payload.prompt: Which statements describe an AI agent?

options.text: It is built on generative AI
options.rationale: An agent is a software application built on generative language capability. That foundation lets it work with natural language.

options.text: It can reason over natural language
options.rationale: An agent can reason over natural language. This is part of how it interprets user requests and prepares responses.

options.text: It can use tools to automate tasks
options.rationale: An agent can use outside capabilities to automate tasks. This is what lets it do more than only respond in language.

options.text: It is only a database of facts
options.error_type: confuses an AI agent with a knowledge source
options.rationale: A database can provide information, but it is not the full agent. An agent also reasons over language, follows instructions, and can act.
options.better_fit: This fits an information source that an agent might access.

feedback.intrinsic: The learner would describe a fact store instead of an assistant that can reason and act.
feedback.instructional: A database can support an agent, but it is not the agent itself. The agent is the broader application that uses reasoning, guidance, and outside capabilities.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. These statements describe the agent as a full application built for language reasoning, task help, and context-based action.

payload.prompt: Which statements correctly describe the model inside an agent?

options.rationale: The large language model is the brain part of the agent. It is responsible for language understanding and reasoning.

options.text: It performs reasoning with generative AI
options.rationale: The model uses generative language capability for reasoning. This supports meaningful responses to prompts.

options.error_type: confuses the model with instructions
options.rationale: The job-description idea describes instructions. The model is the brain for understanding and reasoning.
options.better_fit: This fits instructions, which define role and behavior.

feedback.intrinsic: The learner would mix up the part that reasons with the part that guides behavior.
feedback.instructional: Keep the roles separate: the model reasons, while instructions define what role the agent should follow.

payload.prompt: Which statements correctly describe agent instructions?
